battle.name: 佐賀之亂
battle.theater: 佐賀城下與筑後河沿岸
battle.brief: 一八七四年二月，佐賀士族在江藤新平與島義勇號召下起兵，佔領縣廳與佐賀城，與奉命鎮壓的鎮台兵在筑後河兩岸交鋒。官軍以汽船、電信調度東京、大阪、熊各鎮台步砲兵，雙方裝備同屬雷管步槍一代，勝負卻落在彈藥、砲兵與後勤上。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 這場叛亂的對面是剛完成廢藩置縣、正在推行徵兵制的明治政府，交戰主體是新建成的鎮台兵：大日本帝國陸軍的東京鎮台、大阪鎮台、熊本鎮台與廣島鎮台各出步兵大隊與砲兵分隊，海軍方面有東艦、雲揚、龍驤、鳳翔四艘軍艦，以及存在時間短暫的海兵隊陸戰隊與砲兵。政府方面的指揮系統分三層：太政官決定鎮壓方針並發出徵討令，內務卿大久保利通以捕縛、處刑與兵力鎮撫的全權實際主持軍事，征討總督東伏見宮嘉彰親王於二月二十三日到任坐鎮，本隊作戰則由陸軍少將野津鎮雄指揮。與此同時，九州各地被徵召的舊藩士族組成貫族隊與中立的前山隊，站到政府軍一方作戰。叛亂一方則是分成三派的士族：征韓黨以江藤新平為首，主張以武力推動第二次維新與征韓；憂國黨以島義勇為首，主張回復封建舊制；前山清一郎率領的中立黨多數倒向政府。叛軍編制沿用舊藩的地域團體：憂國黨分勇敢、忠奮、神速、禦侮四個大隊，下轄川久保團、武雄團、多久團、須古團、諫早團；征韓黨原有十五個小隊，後擴至二十五個小隊，兵力來自蓮池、鹿島、小城、白石、唐津等地。兩黨各有司令部，行動上很少協同；武雄領主鍋島茂昌等三支藩與舊藩主鍋島直茂本人都不肯加入。整體而言，這不是兩個國家之間的戰爭，而是同一個新國家內部，一批失去特權的舊武士用新式武器向新軍隊開火。
countriesEn: The other side of this rebellion was the Meiji government, which had just abolished the domains and was putting the new conscription law into effect. The principal fighting force on the government side was the newly created garrison troops of the Imperial Japanese Army, with battalions and artillery detachments drawn from the Tokyo, Osaka, Kumamoto and Hiroshima garrisons; on the naval side there were the four warships Higashi, Unyo, Ryu-yo and Hosh-yo, together with the marines and an artillery detachment of the naval brigade, which itself existed only for a few years. The government command system had three tiers: the Grand Council of State settled the policy of repression and issued the order for punitive expedition; the Home Minister Okubo Toshimichi actually directed the military, holding full authority to arrest, to execute and to pacify by force; and the punitive governor, the prince who was later known as Prince Komatsu Akihito, took up his post on 23 February. Operational command in the field belonged to Major General Nozu Mitsu-o. Alongside the regulars, the samurai of Kyushu were enrolled into units of former retainers, the kanzoku-tai, and the neutral Maeyama detachment, which fought on the government side. The insurgents were likewise divided into three schools. The Seikan-to, headed by Eto Shinpei, wanted a second restoration carried by arms and a march on Korea. The Yukoku-to, headed by Shima Yoshitake, wanted the old feudal order restored. The neutral party of Maeyama Seiichiro came over to the government for the most part. The rebel organisation followed the territorial groups of the old domain: the Yukoku-to was organised into four battalions, the Brave, the Diligent, the Swift and the Resisting, with the Kawakubo, Takeo, Taku, Sugo and Isahaya groups under them, while the Seikan-to began with fifteen detachments, expanded it to twenty-five, and drew its men from Hasunoike, Kashima, Ogi, Shiroishi and Karatsu. The two parties had separate headquarters and seldom acted in concert; the cadet branches of the domain, such as the Takeo lord Nabeshima Shigemasa, and Nabeshima Naoshige himself declined to join. This was not a war between two states but a civil conflict inside a single new country, in which a body of old warriors who had lost their privileges opened fire on the new army with the new weapons.
people: 政府一方最關鍵的人物是內務卿大久保利通：他以文官身分直接掌握兵權，二月十九日在福岡設大本營，二十日令野津鎮雄率領東京鎮台第三砲隊與大阪鎮台第四、第十大隊出動，二十三日把東伏見宮嘉彰親王的征討總督任命、陸軍中將山縣有朋與海軍少將伊東祐麿的參軍任命一併公布，實際上整場戰事由他在東京遙控。野津鎮雄是前線的實際統帥，指揮本隊在朝日山、寒津川、田手川與境原四戰；山田顯義少將守博多，主持三瀨峠方向的戰事；熊本鎮台司令長官谷干城在二月初奉命出動，第十一大隊的左半大隊由參謀山川浩少佐率領走海路，右半大隊由佐久間左馬太少佐率領走陸路，卻因糧秣與彈藥耗盡，在二月十八日夜間突圍時損失三分之一。參謀少佐渡邊央一面接待降服交涉，一面整理出六千三百二十七人的降伏名冊。叛亂一方由兩位黨首並肩：江藤新平二月十三日返抵佐賀並起草決戰之議，前陸軍少佐朝倉尚武在三瀨峠獨力擋住官軍，香月經五郎與石井貞興以縣官身分挪用縣廳公帑與民積金供應火藥，中島鼎藏在寒津川指揮兩翼夾擊官軍本隊。島義勇一度要降，最終仍在副島義高等人力勸下逃向鹿兒島，江藤則轉往土佐。兩人都沒有走到第二步：江藤三月二十九日在甲浦被捕，島義勇三月七日在鹿兒島被捕，四月十三日被斬首梟示，臨時法庭由他早年主持建立的司法制度下的河野敏鎌審判。英國公使哈里·帕克斯在四月二十五日致英國外相的報告中直言，這場鎮壓並未恢復政府的威信，人民反而把刑罰視為對新政權的報復。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the government side was the Home Minister Okubo Toshimichi. Though a civilian, he held the military power directly: he established his headquarters at Fukuoka on 19 February, ordered Major General Nozu Mitsu-o on the 20th to move out with the 3rd Artillery of the Tokyo garrison and the 4th and 10th Battalions of the Osaka garrison, and on the 23rd published the appointment of the prince who later became Prince Komatsu Akihito as punitive governor, together with Lieutenant General Yamagata Aritomo and Rear Admiral Ito Sukeyori as staff officers. The war was in practice run from Tokyo by Okubo alone. Nozu Mitsu-o was the operational commander in the field, directing the main body in the four actions of Asahiyama, Kanzu, Tatemchi and Sakahara; Major General Yamada Akiyoshi held Fukuoka and directed the fighting on the Sanose pass; and the commander of the Kumamoto garrison, Tani Senjiro, was ordered into action at the beginning of February. The 11th Battalion went out in two halves, the left under staff major Yamakawa Hiroshi by sea and the right under staff major Sakuuma Sakyotai by land, and because food and ammunition ran out, a third of the left half was lost when it broke out of the castle on the night of 18 February. Staff major Watanabe Chuo received the surrender negotiations and compiled the roll of 6,327 men who came in. On the rebel side two leaders stood side by side. Eto Shinpei reached Saga on 13 February and drafted the resolve for a decisive battle; the former army major Asakura Naotake held the Sanose pass alone against the government; Kagetsu Kyogoro and Ishii Sadatoki, as prefectural officials, turned the county treasury and the residents' levy money into powder; and Nakajima Teizo directed the pincer on the Kan-etsu river that closed on the government main body. Shima Yoshitake offered to surrender at one point but was carried off toward Kagoshima by his brother and others, while Eto turned to Tosa. Neither got further: Eto was arrested at Ko-ura on 29 March and Shima in Kagoshima on 7 March, and on 13 April both were beheaded and their heads displayed, tried by a temporary court before Kawano Toshiyama, who had served under Eto when the modern judicial system was built. In a despatch to the British Foreign Secretary of 25 April, the British minister Harry Parkes wrote bluntly that the suppression had not restored the authority of the government, and that the people regarded the sentences as revenge against the new regime.
kits: 卡面上這件法國一八四〇年式的雷管步槍，正是這場戰爭裡技術世代的核心。一般認為，日本在一八六八年之後自法國購入M1840式雷管步槍，在國內通稱十八式小銃，它是徵兵令下鎮台步兵的標準裝備；到一八七四年，陸軍已著手把這類底火槍改為螺絲後膛，並在軍需上大量補充恩菲爾步槍的快照彈與莫爾提爾砲。政府軍在九州的火力骨架是砲兵：東京鎮台第三砲隊一百四十四人、大阪鎮台砲兵第七大隊一個小隊一百二十七人，另有熊本鎮台第十一大隊六百四十七人與第十九大隊的一個小隊；大久保在二月二十六日直接向後方請求三十萬打（每打十二發）的恩菲爾步槍彈藥與十三門莫爾提爾砲，彈藥與糧秣由東艦等四艘軍艦、九艘運載船與兩艘租用的英美船共十五艘輸送。步兵以小銃為主，福岡徵集的士族隊員另獲發給小銃與彈藥。叛軍方面的裝備則來自舊藩家底與外援：征韓黨掌權的縣廳在香月經五郎主持下挪用舊佐賀藩武庫的火藥並試圖鑄造大砲，憂國黨與征韓黨的士族攜帶購自海外的洋槍作戰，但彈藥幾乎沒有補充來源，彈藥告罄直接造成朝日山之敗。攻城與守備方面，叛軍在境原挖掘保壘、破壞神埼以南的橋梁遲滯官軍，官軍則靠架橋強渡與砲兵榴散彈壓制保壘。戰場上最直接的物證留在佐賀城鯱之門上，那扇門的門扉至今仍留著當年的彈痕。
kitsEn: The French percussion rifle of 1840 on this card is exactly the technological generation at the centre of this war. Japan is generally held to have bought M1840 percussion rifles from France after 1868 and to have known them at home as the Type 18 rifle, the standard arm of the garrison infantry created by the conscription law; by 1874 the army had begun converting this class of percussion weapon to the screw breech, and was drawing large quantities of Enfield cartridges and mortars on the supply system. The skeleton of government firepower in Kyushu was the artillery: 144 men of the 3rd Artillery of the Tokyo garrison and 127 men of one detachment of the 7th Artillery Battalion of the Osaka garrison, with the 647 men of the 11th Battalion of the Kumamoto garrison and one detachment of the 19th. On 26 February Okubo applied to the rear for 300,000 dozen Enfield cartridges and thirteen mortars, and the ammunition and stores moved by the four warships including Higashi, nine transports and two chartered British and American vessels, fifteen ships in all. The infantry fought with small arms, and the former retainers enlisted from Fukuoka were issued rifles and ammunition of their own. The rebels drew theirs from the old domain and from overseas: under Kagetsu Kyogoro the county authorities that the Seikan-to controlled took the powder from the old Saga arsenal and attempted to cast guns, and the samurai of both parties carried foreign-bought rifles into the field, but there was almost no source of supply, and the running out of ammunition was the direct cause of the defeat at Asahiyama. On attack and defence the rebels dug entrenchments at Sakahara and broke the bridges south of Kanzaki to hold up the government, while the government replied by bridging under fire and crushing the works with canister shot. The most direct relic of the battlefield is in Saga castle: the doors of the shachihoko gate still carry the bullet marks of the fighting.
tactics: 這場戰爭的勝負手不在士氣，而在三樣東西：電信、汽船與彈藥。政府一方把新式的行政與交通當成戰爭的一部分：命令用電報下達，部隊用汽船運送，東京、大阪、熊本的鎮台兵在二月二十日前後分別由海路與陸路趕到九州集結，前線指揮部設在博多，據點之間以傳令與騎兵連繫。戰術上採取正面牽制加側翼包圍：二月二十二日攻擊朝日山時，第四大隊與第三砲隊由轟木道正面推進，第十大隊一半由山浦出側面、一半由宿村迂到背面，三面同時施壓；兩日後在寒津川與田手川，政府軍先以砲兵與步兵交替掩護推進，待第四大隊由北山反轉捅向背後，叛軍全線崩潰；境原之戰則是砲兵以榴散彈砸開保壘、步兵架橋強渡之後兩翼同時夾擊。防守上採海陸分進：第十一大隊左半大隊由海路先入佐賀城，右半大隊由陸路進發，兩部原定會合，卻因糧秣耗盡被迫在二月十八日夜間突圍。叛軍的戰術以拖延與襲擊為主：征韓黨沿長崎街道、憂國黨沿筑後川分線防守，藉保壘與破壞橋梁遲滯官軍，並在官軍宿營時發動千人規模的夜襲；但彈藥不足使他們無法久守。舊佐賀藩曾令全體家臣練習火術與銃陣法，叛軍射手本有底子，卻缺乏連續射擊與補充彈藥的訓練，密集的射擊在這種消耗戰裡很快失效，縣廳機關掌握的糧餉與火藥反而成為雙方爭奪的關鍵。整場戰爭的技術特徵是：新式雷管步槍在雙方手上都有，能打贏的卻是後勤。
tacticsEn: What decided this war was not morale but three things: the telegraph, the steamship and ammunition. The government treated the new machinery of administration and transport as part of the operation. Orders went down by wire, troops moved by steamer, and the garrison battalions of Tokyo, Osaka and Kumamoto were brought together in Kyushu by land and sea around 20 February, the forward headquarters sitting at Hakata and the posts linked by dispatch riders and mounted messengers. Tactically the government combined frontal pressure with envelopment. In the attack on Asahiyama on 22 February, the 4th Battalion and the 3rd Artillery came straight up the Kiroki road, while half the 10th Battalion struck from the flank at Yama-ura and the other half came round by the rear at Shinden-mura, so that pressure was applied on three sides at once. Two days later, at the Kan-etsu and Tatemchi rivers, the government alternated artillery and infantry in a covered advance, and when the 4th Battalion swung round from Kitayama and struck the rebel rear the whole insurgent line collapsed. At Sakahara the artillery opened the entrenchments with canister, the infantry bridged the river under fire, and the two wings closed in together. On defence the government advanced by sea and land separately: the left half of the 11th Battalion entered Saga castle by sea while the right half came by land to join them, but with food and ammunition exhausted the left half was forced to break out on the night of 18 February. The rebel tactics were those of delay and ambush. The Seikan-to held the Nagasaki highway and the Yukoku-to the Chikugo river, using entrenchments and broken bridges to hold up the government, and they launched a night attack of a thousand men against the government camp; but without ammunition they could not hold for long. The old Saga domain had required all its retainers to drill with firearms and to learn line-of-file musket drill, so the rebel marksmen were not without training, yet they had no practice in sustained fire or in the resupply that sustained fire requires, and massed volleys failed quickly in this war of attrition. The grain and powder in the hands of the county administration became the prize both sides fought for. The technical signature of the whole war is this: the new percussion rifle was in the hands of both sides, and what won was logistics.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。時間軸：二月一日憂國黨襲擊官銀預託業者小野組，二月四日太政官命熊本鎮台司令長官谷干城鎮壓，二月五日電報被征韓黨在電信局探知，二月九日大久保利通受命赴九州並獲得捕縛、處刑與兵力鎮撫的全權，二月十三日岩村高俊抵熊、十四日第十一大隊分海陸兩路出動、十五日入佐賀城，十六日清晨開戰，十八日夜左半大隊突圍，十九日大久保抵博多並發布徵討令，二十二日朝日山之戰，二十三日寒津川與田手川之戰，二十七日境原總攻，三月一日官軍入城，戰鬥至此結束。兵力：政府軍總數約五千三百人，其中由福岡與小倉舊藩士族組成、持有小銃與彈藥的貫族隊四千三百餘人；常備部分計東京鎮台第三砲隊一百四十四人、大阪鎮台第四大隊五百七十九人與第十大隊六百三十一人、熊本鎮台第十一大隊六百四十七人，另有海兵隊陸戰隊兩個小隊與砲兵一個小隊；待命的廣島鎮台第十五大隊三個中隊四百九十二人、大阪鎮台第十八大隊七百零四人與近衛步兵第二連隊一千一百七十人。叛軍一方記錄分歧頗大：實際投入的估計在三千至六千人，憂國黨四個大隊按小隊六十至八十人推算約一千七百至二千二百人，征韓黨二十五個小隊約一千五百人，多久團名冊載六百九十人；軍方降伏叛徒概計列六千三百二十七人，戰後裁判認定參與者一萬一千八百二十人，其中獲判無罪者一萬零七百一十三人、有罪者四百一十人。傷亡：政府軍正規軍陣亡一百八十四人、負傷一百七十四人，貫族隊等陣亡二十五人、負傷二十七人；另有國史大辭典記政府軍陣亡約三百五十人。叛軍陣亡一百七十三人、負傷一百六十人。二月十八日突圍時，左半大隊三百三十二人中一百三十七人戰死。佐賀市中館町的乾亨院葬有以熊本鎮台為主的新政府軍戰死者一百零七人。距離上，佐賀市至博多約五十公里，至熊本約一百公里，至鳥棲的朝日山約二十五公里，三瀨峠在佐賀與福岡之間，是分隔兩縣的山口。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The sequence: on 1 February the Yukoku-to raided the Saga branch of the Ono-gumi, a firm that held official deposits; on 4 February the Grand Council ordered Tani Senjiro, commander of the Kumamoto garrison, to pacify the district; on 5 February the Seikan-to learned of the order at the telegraph office; on 9 February Okubo Toshimichi was sent to Kyushu with full authority to arrest, to execute and to pacify by force; on 13 February Iwakura Takatoshi reached Kumamoto, on the 14th the 11th Battalion moved out by sea and by land, and on the 15th entered Saga castle; fighting began before dawn on the 16th; on the night of the 18th the left half broke out; on the 19th Okubo reached Hakata and the order for punitive expedition was issued; Asahiyama was fought on the 22nd, the Kan-etsu and Tatemchi on the 23rd, the general attack at Sakahara on the 27th, and the government entered the castle on 1 March, which ended the fighting. Strength: the government force totalled about 5,300 men, of whom more than 4,300 were former retainers of Fukuoka and Kokura enrolled as the kanzoku-tai and issued with rifles and ammunition. The regular component was the 3rd Artillery of the Tokyo garrison at 144 men, the 4th and 10th Battalions of the Osaka garrison at 579 and 631, and the 11th Battalion of the Kumamoto garrison at 647, with two detachments of marines and one of artillery from the naval brigade; held in reserve were three companies of the 15th Battalion of the Hiroshima garrison at 492 men, the 18th Battalion of the Osaka garrison at 704 and the 2nd Guards Infantry Regiment at 1,170. The rebel figures vary widely: the number actually engaged is put between three and six thousand; the four Yukoku-to battalions work out at between 1,680 and 2,240 on a basis of sixty to eighty men a detachment; the twenty-five Seikan-to detachments come to about 1,500; the roll of the Taku group names 690. The army's own count of surrendered rebels gives 6,327, and the court after the war recognised 11,820 participants, of whom 10,713 were acquitted and 410 convicted. Casualties: on the government side 184 of the regulars killed and 174 wounded, and among the kanzoku-tai and others 25 killed and 27 wounded; the Kokushi Daijiten gives about 350 government dead. On the rebel side 173 killed and 160 wounded. In the breakout of 18 February, 137 of the 332 men of the left half were killed. The Kenkoin in Nakamachi, Saga, holds the graves of 107 government soldiers, chiefly of the Kumamoto garrison. As for distances, Saga city is about fifty kilometres from Hakata, about a hundred from Kumamoto and about twenty-five from Asahiyama at Tosu, and the Sanose pass lies between Saga and Fukuoka as the gap through the mountains.
cause: 要理解這場叛亂，得把明治初年九州士族的處境拆成三層。最上層是政治：征韓論在一八七三年釀成明治六年政變，江藤新平、板垣退助、副島種臣、後藤象二郎與西鄉隆盛五名參議同時下野，江藤回到故鄉佐賀，等於給本地的反政府士族點了一盞燈。征韓黨在一八七三年十二月二十三日成立，骨幹是青年官僚、留學生與現任軍官，開會多在縣衙的弘道館與與賀馬場的延命院；憂國黨則於一八七四年一月集結於佐賀城南的寶琳院，以四十至五十歲的舊藩上層為主，一月十六日徵韓黨以借用為名強要弘道館作集會場所，二月一日憂國黨為俸祿等事襲擊小野組的佐賀分店。第二層是制度：廢藩置縣、徵兵令、秩祿與地租變革同時落到士族身上，舊藩士族既失去世襲的收入，也不再有拒絕徵兵的權力。第三層是生計：這一年佐賀先受乾旱與颱風失收，米價騰貴，天花流行，鄰近筑前又發生竹槍一揆，縣內地主與小作人之間的加地子爭議也讓鄉村不滿累積。真正把三層壓在一起的，是雙方的處置失當：縣令岩村通俊上京後縣的統制鬆動，征韓黨官員香月經五郎與石井貞興掌握縣廳後挪用民積金一萬二千餘圓與舊知事家祿代金二萬五千圓備辦軍資，岩村高俊的傲慢又讓島義勇與他決裂。江藤二月十三日返鄉並起草決戰之議之後，兩黨合流，大家也相信只要佐賀一動，薩摩與土佐的不平士族就會跟進——這正是全案最致命的一項誤判。
causeEn: To understand this rebellion the position of the Kyushu samurai in the early Meiji years has to be taken apart into three layers. The top layer is political. The Seikanron controversy produced the coup of October 1873, and five councillors resigned at once: Eto Shinpei, Itagaki Taisuke, Saigo Takamori, Goto Shojiro and Taneomi Sukenori. Eto's return to his native Saga was in effect a lamp lit for the anti-government samurai of the district. The Seikan-to was founded on 23 December 1873, its backbone made up of young officials, students returned from Europe and serving army and naval officers, and it met in the Kodokan hall of the prefectural offices and afterwards in the Enmyoin in Yaga-mamba. The Yukoku-to gathered in the Horin-in south of Saga castle in January 1874, made up of the upper ranks of the old domain in their forties and fifties. On 16 January the Seikan-to demanded the Kodokan hall in the name of a loan, and on 1 February the Yukoku-to raided the Saga branch of the Ono-gumi over the question of stipends and salaries. The second layer is institutional: the abolition of the domains, the conscription law, the stipend measures and the land tax reform all fell on the samurai at once, so that former retainers lost both the hereditary income and the right to refuse service. The third layer is livelihood: the year brought drought and a typhoon, the harvest failed and the price of rice rose, smallpox was spreading, and the neighbouring province of Chikuzen saw an uprising with bamboo spears, while disputes over the ad valorem rent between landowners and tenant farmers in the county added to rural discontent. What finally pressed the three layers together was mutual mismanagement. After the prefectural governor Iwamura Michitoshi went up to Tokyo, control in the county slackened; once the Seikan-to officials Kagetsu Kyogoro and Ishii Sadatoki had the prefectural administration in their hands they turned some 12,000 yen of the residents' levy money and 25,000 yen of the former governor's stipend payments into war funds; and the arrogance of Iwamura Takatoshi drove Shima Yoshitake into open opposition. When Eto came back on 13 February and drew up the resolve for a decisive battle, the two parties closed ranks, and all of them believed that once Saga rose the discontented samurai of Satsuma and Tosa would follow. That was the most fatal miscalculation in the whole business.
impact: 這場只有一個多月的叛亂，卻改變了明治日本的幾件事。第一，鎮壓手段本身成了樣板：一八七三年徵兵令才施行一年，政府第一次用徵兵來的國民軍去對付自己過去的軍人，並且靠電信與汽船在數日內完成跨海集結。電報第一次成為內戰的決定性工具——命令在二月初就下到熊本，卻早被征韓黨從電信局探知，前線的失誤與混亂因此直接傳到東京；同一種速度也讓政府在二月十七日禁止新聞刊登軍事消息，並在十七個縣禁止販運槍砲彈藥。明治政府由此學會的第一課，是把情報與物資的調度當作戰爭的組成部分。第二，司法的問題被推到前面：四月五日設置的臨時法庭只審兩天，江藤與島義勇等十三人被判死刑，連帶一百三十六人徒刑、二百四十人除族、七人禁固，一萬零七百一十三人無罪；主審的河野敏鎌正是江藤早年建立近代司法制度時的舊部下，江藤本人則是明治司法的奠基者之一，這場只給答辯、不給上訴的審判在後來一直被視為司法獨立的污點，英國公使哈里·帕克斯也在四月二十五日致英國外相的報告裡指出，鎮壓並未恢復政府的威信，人民反而把這場刑罰看作新政權的私怨。第三，士族反亂的路線就此斷了：江藤原本指望薩摩與土佐接應，實際上兩地按兵不動，孤立反而讓政府得以用最硬的手段一次了結；此後九州的士族能量轉向民撰議院建白與自由民權運動，直至一八七七年的西南戰爭才再以另一種形式爆發。值得注意的是，部分參與過佐賀的士族後來仍加入西南戰爭的行列，這條線說明反亂與自由民權之間的分界線從來不如事後論述的那樣清楚。
impactEn: This rebellion, which lasted barely a month, changed several things in Meiji Japan. First, the means of suppression themselves became a model. The conscription law was only a year old, and for the first time the government used a national army raised by conscription to fight the army it had itself been, and it concentrated that force across the sea in a matter of days by wire and by steamer. The telegraph became for the first time a decisive instrument of civil war: the order had gone down to Kumamoto at the beginning of February, but the Seikan-to had already read it at the telegraph office, and the confusion in the line was carried straight back to Tokyo. The same speed also produced censorship, for on 17 February the government forbade the newspapers to print anything about the military operations and banned the sale, carriage and transport of arms, ammunition and powder in seventeen provinces. The first thing the Meiji government learned was that the movement of information and stores was part of the war itself. Second, the question of the courts was pushed to the front. The temporary court set up on 5 April sat for two days and sentenced thirteen men to death, Eto and Shima among them, together with 136 to penal servitude, 240 to loss of status and seven to confinement, while 10,713 were acquitted. The presiding judge, Kawano Toshiyama, had been a subordinate of Eto in the building of the modern judicial system, and Eto himself had been one of the founders of Meiji justice; the trial, which allowed no real defence and no appeal, was afterwards treated as a stain on the independence of the judiciary, and the British minister Harry Parkes wrote to the Foreign Secretary on 25 April that the suppression had not restored the authority of the government and that the people took the sentences as the private revenge of the new regime. Third, the line of armed revolt by the samurai was broken here. Eto had counted on Satsuma and Tosa to join in, and in fact both stayed still; that isolation was exactly what allowed the government to finish the matter in one stroke with the hardest means at its disposal. The energy of the Kyushu samurai then turned to the movement for a national assembly and to the campaign for civil rights, and did not break out again in another form until the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877. It is worth noting that a number of the men who had taken part at Saga later turned up in the ranks of the Satsuma Rebellion, which shows that the line between revolt and the civil rights movement was never as clear as the retrospective account would have it.
result: 結果是政府方的完全勝利，而且是一次以裝備與後勤而不是以名將取勝的勝利。三月一日大久保利通與政府軍進入佐賀城，抵抗結束；江藤在二月二十七日到達鹿兒島，會見西鄉隆盛要求出兵援助被拒，三月十日轉乘漁船經日向與四國北上，三月二十九日在土佐甲浦被捕；島義勇三月七日於鹿兒島被拘，四月十六日押回佐賀。審判自四月五日的臨時法庭開始，十三日江藤新平與島義勇斬首梟示，另十一人斬首，一百三十六人徒刑，二百四十人除族，七人禁固，一萬零七百一十三人宣告無罪。戰後的政治效果同樣清楚：反亂的武裝路線失敗，士族階層在明治國家中的位置被牢牢固定，舊藩的地域團體與私兵時代結束，徵兵令與警察制度把國家對地方的控制伸到町與村；一九一九年因朝鮮皇太子婚約而頒布的特赦令，使江藤等人獲得赦免，一九二〇年本地有志在佐賀市水ヶ江建起慰靈碑，而乾亨院裡以熊本鎮台為主的一百零七名新政府軍戰死者則由另一塊碑收留。從兵器史的角度看，這場戰爭的意義更為具體：卡面上這件法國雷管步槍所代表的技術世代，在一八七四年的九州同時出現在政府的鎮台兵與叛亂的士族手上，雙方裝備的差距並不大，最後決定勝負的卻是彈藥補給、砲兵數量、汽船與電信——這也是日本近代戰爭由藩兵轉為國民軍的第一個實例。
resultEn: The result was a complete victory for the government, and a victory won by equipment and logistics rather than by famous generals. On 1 March Okubo Toshimichi and the government troops entered Saga castle and the resistance was over. Eto reached Kagoshima on 27 February, was refused assistance by Saigo Takamori, and on 10 March took a fishing boat north by way of Hyuga and Shikoku; he was arrested at Ko-ura in Tosa on 29 March. Shima Yoshitake was taken in Kagoshima on 7 March and brought back to Saga on the 16th. The trial opened before the temporary court on 5 April, and on the 13th Eto Shinpei and Shima Yoshitake were beheaded and their heads displayed, with eleven others beheaded, 136 given penal servitude, 240 deprived of status, seven confined, and 10,713 acquitted. The political effect was just as clear: the armed line of samurai revolt had failed, the place of the samurai class in the Meiji state was nailed down, the age of the territorial groups and private armies of the old domains was over, and conscription and the police system carried the control of the state down to town and village. In 1919 an amnesty, following the announcement of the marriage of the Korean crown prince, cleared Eto and his companions; in 1920 the local worthies raised a memorial to the fallen at Mizu-gae in the city of Saga, while a second stone in the Kenkoin holds the hundred and seven government soldiers, chiefly of the Kumamoto garrison. Seen from the history of arms the meaning of the war is more specific still: the technological generation represented by the French percussion rifle on this card stood in the hands of both the government garrisons and the rebel samurai in Kyushu in 1874, and the gap in equipment between the two sides was not large. What decided it was ammunition supply, the weight of artillery, steamers and telegraph. This was also the first instance of Japanese modern war passing from the armies of the domains to a national army raised by conscription.
